name: mobile_de_search_chromium
description: EXPECT THE RATE TO MOVE: mobile.de sits behind Akamai Bot Manager, and how often it admits us is a property of exit reputation on the day, not of this recipe. Measured through the presets as shipped: 1 of 4 attempts on 2026-09-06, then 7 of 8 on 2026-09-11 (chromium 4/4, camoufox 3/4; medians 56 s and 28 s end to end). Do not read either number as the rate -- re-measure before building anything that needs a first-attempt success. A refused run ends on an Akamai page at HTTP 200 with empty columns; that is the site refusing the exit, not a broken recipe, and whenever the page arrives every column fills. mobile.de car listings (Germany) for a make/model pair, by mobile.de's own numeric ids (`make_id`, `model_id` -- e.g. 3500/20 = BMW 525; the ids are the ones its filter form submits as makeModelVariant1.makeId/modelId). Returns one flat array per field across result cards; consumers zip them by index. ROW-ALIGNMENT INVARIANT: each field matches exactly one node per card, so every optional value is dug out of the per-card container's html by regex and a card without it yields null in its slot instead of shrinking the column and shifting every row after it. mobile.de's class names are build hashes (_NzmyG, _CoixB ...); every selector anchors on the `data-testid` hooks (listing-title-card-view, main-price-label, listing-details-attributes, sponsored-badge) inside the per-listing card, which is the `<a href=…/fahrzeuge/details.html?id=…>` wrapping the whole listing (title, price and attributes all sit inside it, measured 24 of 24 cards); `urls` keep the ad id and drop the per-session `searchId`/`refId`/`ref=srp` tail. Every listing is the site's own query-addressed page on one path, so the preset declares `links_stay_on_site` and the worker's self-referential-links guard, which counts distinct paths, does not report a healthy page as an unwrapped redirect. `prices` read "3.750 €" (dot-grouped) as 3750.0; `details` is the attribute line as printed ("EZ 01/2008 • 256.000 km • 160 kW (218 PS) • Benzin"); `sponsored` is an always-present marker ("sponsored-badge" on a Gesponsert card, "" otherwise; 4 of 24 marked on the capture). The site sits behind Akamai Bot Manager: a first navigation gets a 227-byte sensor shell (HTTP 200, `location.reload` after the sensor runs). What lets the page through is a warmup of https://www.mobile.de/ (the target origin suchen.mobile.de seeds nothing); through the presets as shipped both twins passed about 1 attempt in 4 (see ENGINE below). Both twins carry the warmup because without it nothing passed. ENGINE: Chromium (real Chrome, headful). Raw probes on this URL: the www warmup passed with stealth on (1 of 1) and failed with stealth off (1 of 1), the target-origin warmup did the reverse (off 1 of 1 on its second attempt, on 0 of 1), and on the ad page the www warmup passed with both -- Akamai admits some attempts and not others, stealth made no consistent difference, and the www warmup is the setting under which 3 of 4 raw attempts across both pages passed -- but through the presets as shipped later the same day both twins passed about 1 attempt in 4 (see ENGINE below). MEASURED 2026-09-06 through the preset as shipped, LOW: 0 of 6 runs (two concurrent, four one-at-a-time; every attempt ended on the Akamai shell, 105-111 s spent on three attempts each; research/preset_audit_new_bases_2026_09_06.json + …_seq_…). The probes earlier the same day passed 2 of 4 attempts on this URL with the same settings, so this is a per-attempt lottery that got worse as the day's probing went on -- read it as exit/fingerprint reputation at Akamai, not as a selector or budget problem (the recipe extracts 24 of 24 listings whenever the page arrives). Re-measure on a fresh day before relying on it. timeout_ms 31000 (per-phase, with the 10 s warmup dwell; see test_builtin_timeout_fits_the_first_attempt). SCOPE FIX (review 2026-09-08): the card anchor was matched anywhere on the document, so a 'similar vehicles' block or a footer link to an ad would have added rows -- polluting the result set, and misaligning it outright for any such link that carries no title node. Every column is now scoped to `[data-testid='result-list']`. On the 2026-09-06 capture this changes nothing (all 24 anchors already sit inside the list), which is the point: it is a guard, not a repair. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-11 through the preset as shipped: 7 of 8 across both twins (chromium 4/4, camoufox 3/4 -- the one failure was NS_BINDING_ABORTED on navigation, not the Akamai page). Five days after the 09-06 run and on the same pool, which is the evidence that the rate tracks exit reputation.
